dedupe_keys.name: us national security memorandum 22 on critical infrastructure security and resilience 2024 and dhs 2024 2025 strategic guidance

description: National Security Memorandum 22, issued on 30 April 2024, replaced Presidential Policy Directive 21 as the US policy on critical infrastructure security and resilience. It makes the Secretary of Homeland Security the national coordinator, sets roles for Sector Risk Management Agencies, calls for minimum risk management requirements, analysis of dependencies and interdependencies among assets and systems and management of systemic and cross-sector risk, and establishes a two-year risk management cycle with sector plans and a biennial National Infrastructure Risk Management Plan. Under it, the DHS Secretary issued strategic guidance on 14 June 2024 for the 2024 to 2025 cycle, naming priority risk areas: cyber and other threats from the People's Republic of China, artificial intelligence and emerging technology, supply chain vulnerabilities, climate risks, and growing dependence on space systems, plus resilience, baseline requirements, service provider incentives and concentrated risk. The memorandum text is free on the American Presidency Project and the guidance is a free DHS PDF. Caveats: these are policy texts without data, and later administrations may revise them. They support framing of cross-sector and systemic risk scenarios for infrastructure interdependency models; a related record is the US National Infrastructure Protection Plan.
